summary: RBAC + Marketplace endpoints & role-based routing (iteration_9). Backend: 30/30 pytest PASSED in /app/backend/tests/test_rbac_marketplace.py — covers (a) /auth/me role for admin/driver/facility/dispatcher; (b) POST /jobs role gating (driver 403, facility/dispatcher/admin 200); (c) GET /jobs scoping: driver sees only open + own assigned jobs and posted_by is stripped via DRIVER_JOB_FIELDS whitelist, facility sees only own posted/facility_id jobs, dispatcher & admin see all; (d) driver verification gating: fresh driver (POST /auth/register, no driver record) 403 on POST /jobs/{id}/accept with 'verification' in detail; driver1 (approved) accepts+completes ok with commission ledger; (e) PUT /jobs/{id}: assigning unverified driver→400 'driver verification is not approved'; assigning verified driver1 syncs accepted_by; status=offered without driver→400; driver assigned to job can PUT status only (payout_amount→403 'Drivers can only update job status'); (f) audit logs: driver/facility→403 on GET /audit-logs, dispatcher & admin→200; every create writes audit_logs entry with actor_id, actor_role, action='create', entity='job', entity_id, timestamp; (g) GET /facilities: driver response lacks billing_email, facility sees only own (with billing_email), admin & dispatcher see with billing_email; (h) GET /drivers works for dispatcher (staff), 403 for driver/facility; (i) regression: driver1 accept→in_progress→complete flow + commission ledger entry still green. Frontend Playwright: (1) facility login lands /facility with facility-home + role-home-user-name 'Facility One (facility)' + 'Facility Portal' heading + role-home-logout-btn; guards: /dashboard & /admin redirect back to /facility. (2) dispatcher login lands /dispatch with dispatch-home + 'Dispatch Console'; guard: /jobs redirects to /dispatch. (3) driver login lands /dashboard; guard: /admin redirects to /dashboard. (4) admin login lands /admin. Logout button clears session and redirects to /login. No bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 2033 lines — monolith continues to grow (iteration_8 flagged 1388). Split into routers/jobs.py, routers/facilities.py, routers/audit.py, routers/rbac.py at minimum. Refactor overdue and will slow future iterations.

server.py log_audit is best-effort but never wrapped in try/except; if audit_logs insert fails (e.g. disk full) the whole business op (create/update/accept) will 500 even though the actual job write succeeded. Wrap log_audit in try/except and log at ERROR level so compliance logging never breaks the request path.

server.py L1300, 1310, 1319 log_audit(entity='job', entity_id='list') — writing 'list' as entity_id for view actions is a code smell. Either use a NULL/omit entity_id for list ops, or store the query filter. As-is, filtering audit-logs by entity_id='list' returns a wall of noise.

server.py PUT /jobs L1907 driver-field restriction uses `set(updates.keys()) - {'status'}` AFTER validate_* calls have already been made with the driver's payload. Not a security issue but the driver's rejected fields still trigger validation errors first (e.g. driver sends bogus item_category → 400 instead of 403). Move the driver-only-status check earlier.
server.py PUT /jobs L1911-1917: verification check on assigned_driver_id is duplicated with the check on target_driver for offered/accepted status. Consolidate.

server.py L1295 driver query: `{'$or':[{'status':'open'}, {'accepted_by': uid}, {'assigned_driver_id': uid}]}` — no index hinted; production data will scan. Add compound indexes on jobs.status, jobs.accepted_by, jobs.assigned_driver_id, jobs.posted_by, jobs.facility_id.

server.py DELETE /jobs/{id} L1944 lets any user with posted_by == self delete a job — but a facility user could delete a job posted by ADMIN on behalf of their facility_id (since owner_user_id check is only on posted_by, not facility_id). Should also allow facility user to delete jobs where facility_id in facility_ids_owned_by(user).

server.py facilities L1836 strip_facility_billing pipeline: staff always see billing_email; owner sees it; everyone else stripped — good. But GET /facilities/{id} for a driver returns billing_email if the driver happens to be the owner_user_id (edge case, unlikely but possible). Consider whitelisting fields for drivers globally like DRIVER_JOB_FIELDS instead of only stripping billing_email.
FacilityHomePage & DispatchHomePage are near-identical (46 lines each). Extract a shared RoleHomeShell component that takes {icon, title, description} props.
AuthContext.js still keeps token in localStorage (bearer). Cookie/httpOnly auth path noted in auth_testing.md not implemented — not in scope for this iteration but flagged for security review.

App.js RoleRoute allows 'admin' as a fallback role for /facility, /dispatch, /dashboard, /jobs (admin can view everyone's home) — intentional, but means admin visiting /facility renders 'Facility One (facility)' user context — actually renders admin's own user with role 'admin'. Placeholder page shows role in the header so admin sees '(admin)' next to their name on a Facility Portal shell — mildly confusing UX. Consider blocking admin from these role-placeholder homes, or add a note that the admin is 'viewing as'.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (4 role-login flows + 4 route-guard flows + logout all green)

context_for_next_testing_agent: RBAC feature-set is fully functional end-to-end. Reusable regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_rbac_marketplace.py — set env with `export $(grep -v '^#' /app/frontend/.env | xargs)` before pytest (test file reads REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL). Key gotchas discovered: (1) POST /api/facilities REQUIRES contact_name + contact_phone; status enum is ['approved','pending','suspended'] NOT 'active'. (2) Fresh driver from POST /api/auth/register default role is 'driver' with NO drivers record — perfect for verification-gating tests. (3) audit-logs writes entity_id='list' for view-list actions; filter by entity_id=<jobId> to get per-job audit. (4) driver's own accept flow still uses legacy 'in_progress' status (not the marketplace status set) — intentional per problem statement. (5) PUT /api/jobs/{id} treats assigned_driver_id assignment and status=offered independently — assigning driver alone is fine even without status change. (6) roleHome() in AuthContext.js maps admin→/admin, facility→/facility, dispatcher→/dispatch, else→/dashboard. Placeholder pages have data-testid=facility-home / dispatch-home + role-home-user-name + role-home-logout-btn.
rca of the issue: No bugs found. All 10 review items from the problem statement pass. Full audit trail on jobs, correct role-based data scoping, correct route guards, correct driver verification gating.
